solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Person helping parents out, whose charges are small

definitions.meaning: reads like a charity worker or relative giving support to a family
charges can be fees, but here they are the children in someone's care, who are little

explanation.surface: Someone offering a hand to parents who keeps their fees modest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' suggests low prices; the real sense is the young ones being looked after.
explanation.definitionFit: A person minding children while the parents go out is exactly this kind of helper.

clue.text: Epitome of soundness or beauty, say

indicators.note: say tells us to take the word for beauty as it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A query about what best represents health or good looks.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'as sound as a bell' makes the bell the model of soundness.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'sound as a bell' makes this ringing object the proverbial standard of being in perfect condition.

clue.text: It supports complaint about new type of welfare

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits underneath, so the word It comes last
the word for complaint wraps around the abbreviation for new

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or grievance
taken as written

explanation.surface: Grumbling about a new kind of state handout.
explanation.definitionFit: State payments such as unemployment or child allowance are paid out as part of a welfare system.

clue.text: Track Conservative support around popular would-be ministers

parts.note: to shadow someone is to follow or track them

indicators.note: the word for support goes round the word for popular

parts.note: to abet is to help or support
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A political story of following a Tory who backs fashionable hopefuls for office.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics the opposition party's team of spokespeople mirrors the government ministers they hope to replace.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposition's senior team, waiting to take over government posts, are ministers in waiting.

clue.text: With little time left, Germany finally score

parts.note: T is the short form of time
went, as in departed

indicators.note: only the closing letter of Germany is used

parts.note: the word whose last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A football report: with seconds remaining, the Germans score at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like a goal, but it is the old word for a set of twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is an old counting unit equal to twenty, as in 'threescore years and ten'.

clue.text: Performer I put under pressure in next upset

indicators.note: the combined pieces sit inside the rearranged letters
upset means the letters of next are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry the word for I sits beneath the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
I is the Roman numeral one, written here as the word

explanation.surface: A worried performer, stressed about whoever goes on stage after them.
explanation.definitionFit: An exponent of an art is a practitioner who performs or demonstrates it.

clue.text: Assistance needed to consume cold tart

indicators.note: the word for help takes in, or swallows, the cold letter

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: A cold pastry needs help being eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' is not a pastry but an adjective meaning sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a sharp, sour taste, as with vinegar or lemon.

clue.text: Cat he repeatedly tormented becomes wild feline

indicators.note: tormented means twisted and tortured, so the gathered letters are wrenched into a new order
repeatedly means the little word he is written out a second time

explanation.surface: A cat that a man keeps tormenting turns savage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' gives HEHE; with CAT, 'tormented' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The fastest land animal, a spotted African big cat, is an untamed member of the cat family.

clue.text: Passed over small pamphlet, not paying attention

indicators.note: the word for passed covers, or goes over, the other pieces in this down entry

parts.note: to pass away is to die
a tract is a short religious or political pamphlet

explanation.surface: Someone skipped over a little leaflet because they weren't concentrating.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose thoughts have wandered elsewhere is not focused, so inattentive.

clue.text: Descent taking long time on rope

indicators.note: the long time is placed on, after, the rope

parts.note: a line is a rope, as on a ship
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A climber's slow abseil, taking ages to come down a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Descent' looks like climbing down; here it means ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: One's descent is one's ancestry or family line, the same as pedigree.

clue.text: Sheets put on piano for musicians

indicators.note: the sheets are placed on, after, the piano letter

parts.note: layers, as sheets laid one on another

explanation.surface: Covering a piano with dust sheets before the band arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: People who play instruments are performers, the plural noun matching musicians.

clue.text: Notice conclusions of judge for court, given careful consideration outside

indicators.note: the word for consideration goes around the final letters

parts.note: advisement is deliberation, as in taking a matter under advisement

indicators.note: the last letter of each of the three words is taken

parts.note: the three words whose ends are used

explanation.surface: A legal notice: the judge's verdicts for the court, weighed with care.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice publicising something is a public announcement, the same as an ad.

clue.text: To travel in fog is stupid for indecisive citizen

indicators.note: the phrase is stupid suggests the letters are muddled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Driving through thick mist is foolish, a warning to any undecided traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: An elector who has not settled on a party before polling day is uncommitted.

clue.text: Holder of money, with rest foolishly invested in financial centre

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are put inside the money holder

parts.note: a wallet holds cash

indicators.note: the letters of rest are arranged foolishly, out of order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly sinks the rest of their purse into the stock market.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York street housing the stock exchange is shorthand for the American finance industry.

clue.text: Where last flight goes? Area that's part of Greece

parts.note: the top flight of stairs leads up to the roof space

explanation.surface: Where does the final plane head? To a region of Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last flight' suggests an aircraft; it is the top flight of stairs in a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The region around Athens is a historic Greek district, the peninsula of the city-state.

clue.text: Section of Roman arch I constructed, following no rules

indicators.note: only a section of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of Roman, all of arch and I, and the start of constructed

explanation.surface: Part of a Roman archway I built, put up without regard to regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawless, chaotic behaviour with no authority or order is how the adjective is used.

clue.text: Medium spoke, produced speech hard to follow

parts.note: uttered means said or spoke

explanation.surface: A spiritualist spoke at a séance in words no one could understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' suggests a psychic, but it gives only its abbreviation M, as in clothing sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking low and indistinctly so listeners struggle to catch the words is mumbling.

clue.text: Before a contest, amateur is slacker

indicators.note: the amateur word comes before the rest

parts.note: lay means non-professional, as in a layman
taken as written
a bout is a fight or contest

explanation.surface: An amateur boxer lazing about before a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: An idle person who avoids work is a loafer or shirker.

clue.text: Rabbiting with bovine creature on non-subject

indicators.note: in a down entry the animal sits on top of the other piece

parts.note: a yak is a Himalayan ox
a king rules his subjects and is not one himself

explanation.surface: Chattering away with an ox about nothing in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit (on) is British slang for to talk at length.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for chattering on and on, talking a lot about little.

clue.text: Record's extremely short

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the official written note of a meeting
second meaning: tiny, said with stress on the second syllable

explanation.surface: An athletics record that was only just set.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the written note of a meeting; the adjective, pronounced differently, means tiny.

clue.text: Experience inferior to travel

parts.note: under, as in ranking under someone
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Feeling outclassed when on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through or suffer something, such as surgery, is to experience it.

clue.text: Central part of argument always in mind

indicators.note: the letters come from the middle of the phrase, losing its outer letters

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of argument and the start of always

explanation.surface: The heart of a debate is always intellectual.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taking place in the head, such as arithmetic, is a cerebral or psychological matter.

clue.text: Having a major role in stealing valuable stuff from church

parts.note: taking, as in taking what is not yours
lead is often stripped from church roofs by thieves for its scrap value

explanation.surface: Thieves stripping metal from a church roof.
explanation.walkthrough: Theft of lead roofing from churches is a well-known crime in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in front and directing things is the idiom for heading up an effort.

clue.text: Line taken from almost endless prophetic book

indicators.note: the letter is removed from the word that follows
without its end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove a line from a nearly unending book of prophecy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts ALMOST to ALMOS, and 'taken from' removes the L for line.
explanation.definitionFit: It names one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament and the scriptural text bearing his name.

clue.text: European champion who puts people out?

parts.note: a victor is a winner

explanation.surface: A European title-winner who knocks opponents out.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads like a sporting knockout; it means turning tenants out of a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who removes occupants from a property, legally expelling them, is described here.

clue.text: Mathematical work, product of mine, seized by our opponents

indicators.note: the mined product is held inside the word for opponents

parts.note: them, as opposed to us
ore is the raw rock dug from a mine

explanation.surface: A rival side grabbing the output of our mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposition proved by mathematical reasoning is a key result in geometry or algebra.

clue.text: Middle of historic game in East African country

indicators.note: only the two central letters of historic are used

parts.note: the word whose two central letters are taken
go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A traditional sport played in an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Togo is actually in West Africa, on the Gulf of Guinea, so 'East' is the setter's slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Togo is a small nation in Africa, lying between Ghana and Benin.

clue.text: Absurdly old, a suitor not operating in good faith?

indicators.note: absurdly signals the letters are put together in a ridiculous new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly wooer behaving absurdly and dishonestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good faith' suggests honesty, but the definition plays on religious faith: worshipping false gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Worshipping images rather than the true God is a departure from proper religious belief.
